title: Introduce efficiency-lattice batch shaper and tenant quantization handoff
author: Asha Menon
release_notes: Adds latency-aware batch shaping (efficiency-lattice) and a tenant-scoped quantization handoff gate. Includes a dry-run CLI for unit-econ simulation and telemetry hooks for rollout monitoring.
description:
Motivation: Many tenants exhibit bimodal latency/cost tradeoffs where aggressive batching reduces unit cost but spikes tail latency for interactive routes. This PR implements an "efficiency-lattice" batch shaper that maintains per-tenant batch shape profiles (sequence-length distribution, prefilling ratio, tail-latency percentile targets) and performs a runtime handoff to tenant-specific quantized model variants when throughput vs quality/latency tradeoffs cross configured thresholds.

What changed (high level): - Introduces efficiency-lattice controller (runtime) to compute and apply batch shaping heuristics per-tenant. - Adds tenant-quantization handoff gating with safety checks (accuracy smoke checks, fallback window). - CLI tool redwood-econ-dryrun to simulate traffic traces against candidate batch/quant configs and produce unit-econ estimates and risk profiles. - Telemetry: new metrics (shaper.applied_profile, handoff.attempt, handoff.fallback_count, econ.estimated_cost_tokens) and dashboards in console. - Tests & infra: end-to-end smoke harness, deterministic simulator for CI, feature flag gating.

Why this is unique: Instead of a single global default the lattice supports multiple stable operating points and a decision boundary that chooses conservative vs aggressive shapes by workload signature. The quantization handoff is tenant-scoped and gated by short A/B validation and a warmstart period to limit regressions.

Checklist: - [x] Runtime: scheduling and batcher integration - [x] Safety: fallback path and revert logic - [x] CLI: dry-run mode and summary report - [x] Telemetry: metrics + dashboard skeleton - [x] Tests: simulator unit tests + e2e smoke - [x] Docs: developer guide + ops runbook

Testing performed: Ran redwood-econ-dryrun on three production-sampled traces (chat, search, summarization). Simulated 48-hour traffic windows with and without handoff. Observed median unit cost reduction 12%-18% on aggressive profiles with tail-latency P99 increase < 10ms for interactive tenants in conservative lattice bands. CI flake fixed (simulator seed handling).

Rollout plan: Feature-flagged rollout; step 1: internal beta (canary tenants), step 2: opt-in tenants via console, step 3: automated advisor recommends profiles for eligible tenants after 72h of stable telemetry. Manual rollback via feature flag or immediate fallback if handoff.fallback_count > 5 within 10m.

Related: Linear ENG-2930 (efficiency lattice design), ENG-3001 (economics CLI).

Author (Asha): Renamed metrics and updated dashboard JSON accordingly.

testing_instructions: Build the binary 'make econ-dryrun' then run './bin/redwood-econ-dryrun --trace examples/cli/trace_samples.json --profile conservative,aggressive --out report.json'. Validate report.json contains unit_econ and risk_profiles. For e2e, enable feature flag 'efficiency_lattice' for a canary tenant and replay a 1h sampled trace in staging.
notes_for_ops: Enable feature flag scoped to canary tenants. Watch metrics econ.shaper.* and handoff.*; abort rollout if handoff.fallback_count spikes or econ.estimated_cost_tokens increases unexpectedly. Ops runbook in docs/ops/efficiency_lattice.md
